poolReview.rationale: An immediately repeatable perceptual puzzle resolves into a meaningful distinction between optical images and conscious perception.

candidates.subject: Why you normally cannot see your own rapid eye movements in a mirror
candidates.novelty: A mirror seems to conceal movement that another observer can see.
candidates.evidenceFeasibility: Human suppression studies, stimulus perception exceptions and author neuroscience synthesis support qualified mechanism.
candidates.explanatoryPayoff: Understand how simultaneous looking and moving, rapid retinal motion, reduced sensitivity and visual masking differ from watching a recording afterward.
candidates.visualPotential: One person, one mirror, coherent eye macro, subjective view and separately labeled recorded view.
candidates.audienceCuriosity: Why does the mirror appear to skip a real movement?
candidates.productionFeasibility: Original animated portrait and optical/perceptual illustrations; existing local narration and fonts.
candidates.portfolioDiversity: Owner-selected everyday perception; no category preference.
candidates.comparison: Owner explicitly selects; no fabricated selection pool.
limitations: Ordinary conditions only; altered visual conditions can reveal intrasaccadic motion.
Animation is an illustration, not a psychophysical measurement or literal screen capture of subjective vision.

curiosityReview.honestPremise: Why you normally cannot see your own rapid eye movements in a mirror
curiosityReview.coldAudienceReason: Viewers can test the gap between their direct experience and a recorded external observation.
curiosityReview.storyRoute: Try mirror → later playback reveals movement → saccade → simultaneous moving and looking → retinal sweep → sensitivity loss and masking → no total blindness → playback timing → optical/perceptual payoff.

truthBoundary.rationale: Never becomes normally. Suppression and masking both considered; no black interval or deleted time.

opportunityJudgment.rationale: A small everyday demonstration exposes a consequential property of perception.

rationale: Follow explicit selected-topic V1 authority with independent factual verification.
